meta.trial_name: SHARP (Study of Heart and Renal Protection)
meta.drug: simvastatin 20 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg (fixed-dose combination, VYTORIN 10/20) vs placebo
meta.sponsor: University of Oxford (CTSU); funded mainly by Merck/Schering-Plough, with NHMRC Australia, British Heart Foundation, UK MRC
meta.mechanism: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (simvastatin) plus NPC1L1 cholesterol-absorption inhibitor (ezetimibe); lowers LDL-C (~0.85 mmol/L ITT average, ~1.1 mmol/L at 1 year)
meta.indication: prevention of major atherosclerotic events in moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease (dialysis and non-dialysis) without known MI or coronary revascularisation

n_randomized.quote: Overall, 9270 patients were randomly assigned to simvastatin plus ezetimibe (4650 patients, 4193 initially plus 457 after 1 year) versus placebo (4620 patients, 4191 initially plus 429 after 1 year; figure 1).
n_randomized.note: Main comparison population (simvastatin+ezetimibe 4650 vs placebo 4620). Total randomized into SHARP = 9438 (registry S3 enrollment 9438 ACTUAL; design paper S4 'A total of 9,438 CKD patients were randomized'), including a 1-year simvastatin-only arm (4:4:1) whose members were rerandomized after 1 year (886 of them entered the main comparison).

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up was 4·9 years for surviving patients.

primary_endpoint.value: First major atherosclerotic event: non-fatal MI or coronary death, non-haemorrhagic stroke, or any arterial revascularisation (excluding dialysis access), all patients ever randomized to simvastatin+ezetimibe vs placebo. Original protocol primary: major vascular events in initially randomized patients.
primary_endpoint.quote: The key prespecified outcome was first major atherosclerotic event (non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary death, non-haemorrhagic stroke, or any arterial revascularisation procedure).
primary_endpoint.note: Endpoint change: S1 Methods 'For the reasons given in the statistical analysis plan published before unmasking,12 the steering committee decided that the key study outcome should be changed to major atherosclerotic events ... and the key comparison should be between all patients ever allocated simvastatin plus ezetimibe versus placebo'. Merck release S2 still calls major vascular events (initially randomized) 'the pre-specified primary endpoint'; registry S3 lists major atherosclerotic events as primary and the original major vascular events outcome as secondary.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Age >=40; CKD with >1 previous creatinine >=150 umol/L (1.7 mg/dL) men or >=130 umol/L (1.5 mg/dL) women, on dialysis or not; no known history of MI or coronary revascularisation; no statin use (contraindicated drug)
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients aged 40 years and older were eligible to participate if they had chronic kidney disease with more than one previous measurement of serum or plasma creatinine of at least 150 μmol/L (1·7 mg/dL) in men or 130 μmol/L (1·5 mg/dL) in women, whether receiving dialysis or not.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Exclusions from registry S3: 'Definite history of myocardial infarction or coronary revascularization procedure'; 'Functioning renal transplant, or living donor-related transplant planned'; current statin listed among contraindicated drugs. Eligibility did not depend on lipid level (S7: 'Eligibility did not depend on lipid levels.'). 3023 (33%) on dialysis; non-dialysis mean eGFR 26.6 mL/min/1.73m2.

planned_events.unit: events (major vascular events, original key outcome)
planned_events.quote: A study with at least 1100 such events and all patients followed up for at least 4 years was estimated to have 90% power to detect a 20% proportional reduction at p<0·01.
planned_events.note: Sizing was on the original outcome (major vascular events, projected ~3.7%/year), not on the final key outcome (major atherosclerotic events). Observed: 1145 major atherosclerotic events; 1515 major vascular events (701+814) in all randomized.

assumed_rrr.quote: A study with at least 1100 such events and all patients followed up for at least 4 years was estimated to have 90% power to detect a 20% proportional reduction at p<0·01.
assumed_rrr.note: 20% proportional reduction in major vascular events.

power.quote: A study with at least 1100 such events and all patients followed up for at least 4 years was estimated to have 90% power to detect a 20% proportional reduction at p<0·01.

alpha.quote: A study with at least 1100 such events and all patients followed up for at least 4 years was estimated to have 90% power to detect a 20% proportional reduction at p<0·01.
alpha.note: Power was computed 'at p<0·01'. The final significance threshold in the statistical analysis plan (design paper S4) was not read; S1 says log-rank methods 'to calculate two-sided p values'. Sidedness of the 0.01 not stated explicitly; see open_questions.

stopped_early.quote: participants were to be seen in the study clinics for routine follow-up checks and blood safety monitoring at 2, 6, and 12 months, and then every 6 months for at least 4 years in total, until the final follow-up visits between March and August, 2010.
stopped_early.note: Ran to scheduled completion (registry S3 primary completion 2010-08 ACTUAL).

baseline.unit: mmol/L (mean, placebo; 2.77 active), directly measured, non-fasting
baseline.quote: Mean baseline non-fasting plasma concentrations were 4·9 (SD 1·2) mmol/L for total cholesterol, 2·8 (SD 0·9) mmol/L for directly measured LDL cholesterol, 1·1 (SD 0·3) mmol/L for HDL cholesterol, and 2·3 (SD 1·7, IQR 1·3–2·8) mmol/L for triglycerides (table 1).
baseline.note: Table 1: LDL-C 2.77 (0.88) simvastatin+ezetimibe vs 2.78 (0.87) placebo mmol/L. Merck S2: 'the average LDL cholesterol of all patients enrolled in SHARP was 108 mg/dL'. Lower on dialysis: 'Mean LDL cholesterol concentration was lower in patients on dialysis than in those who were not (2·6 [SD 0·9] vs 2·9 [SD 0·9] mmol/L; p<0·0001).'
NOT FOUND: baseline apoB not reported in the main text (webappendix not accessed).
NOT FOUND: baseline non-HDL-C not reported (TC 4.9 minus HDL-C 1.1 = 3.8 mmol/L is a derived difference of means, not a reported value).

baseline.quote: mean blood pressure was 139/79 mm Hg

biomarker_effects.timepoint: average over follow-up (study midpoint, 2.5 years; 26-31 months)
biomarker_effects.method: direct LDL-C, central lab, non-fasting; ITT with missing values imputed from baseline (assumes non-compliance)
biomarker_effects.quote: As a result, the intention-to-treat comparisons assess the effects of around two-thirds of participants actually taking LDL-cholesterol-lowering treatment daily, which yielded an average LDL cholesterol difference of 0·85 mmol/L (SE 0·02; table 2).
biomarker_effects.note: Absolute -0.85 mmol/L (SE 0.02) from S1. Percent -30 from Merck release S2: 'After two and half years of treatment, which was approximately mid-way through the study, VYTORIN lowered LDL cholesterol by 32 mg/dL, or 30 percent from baseline, compared to placebo.' The 2012 FDA-label release S7 says 32% ('At the mid-point of the study (2.5 years), the mean LDL cholesterol was 32 percent lower for VYTORIN relative to placebo.'). Derived check 0.85/2.78 = 31%. Diluted by ~61% net difference in LDL-lowering drug use (71% vs 9% at midpoint). Smaller on dialysis: 0.60 vs 0.96 mmol/L non-dialysis (S1). Authors: with full compliance ~1.3 mmol/L. CTT check (derived, not from source): 0.78^0.85 = 0.81 expected vs observed 0.83.

biomarker_effects.quote: Compared with placebo, allocation to ezetimibe 10 mg plus simvastatin 20 mg daily yielded average LDL cholesterol differences of 43 mg/dL (1.10 mmol/L) at 1 year and 33 mg/dL (0.85 mmol/L) at 2.5 years.
biomarker_effects.note: Design/baseline paper published 2010-09-18, i.e. BEFORE the readout: the midpoint LDL-C difference was public before the outcome. S2 gives 32 mg/dL. Percent from S2.

biomarker_effects.method: direct LDL-C, central lab (~10% sample at 1 year); ITT
biomarker_effects.note: Table 2 row '8–13 months': drug use 77% vs 3%; LDL-C change -1.08 vs 0.02; absolute difference -1.09 (SE 0.06) mmol/L (table, no prose quote). Design paper S4: 1.10 mmol/L (43 mg/dL) at 1 year. Percent -40 from S2 ('In the first year of the trial, VYTORIN 10/20 mg lowered LDL cholesterol by 40 percent compared to placebo, while simvastatin 20 mg lowered LDL cholesterol by 28 percent versus placebo'); S7 gives 38% (VYTORIN) and 26% (simvastatin) at 1 year. At 44-49 months: -0.77 (SE 0.06) mmol/L (Table 2).

biomarker_effects.timepoint: 12 months (phase 2 pilot UK-HARP-I, simvastatin 20 mg alone vs placebo)
biomarker_effects.quote: allocation to 20 mg of simvastatin daily reduced nonfasting total cholesterol levels by 18% (simvastatin, 163 mg/dL [4.22 mmol/L] versus placebo, 196 mg/dL [5.08 mmol/L]; P < 0.0001), directly measured low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by 24% (89 mg/dL [2.31 mmol/L] versus 114 mg/dL [2.96 mmol/L]; P < 0.0001)
biomarker_effects.note: n=448 CKD patients (predialysis, dialysis, transplant). Absolute -0.65 mmol/L is derived (2.96-2.31), not reported as a difference. Simvastatin component only. Published 2005, before readout.

biomarker_effects.timepoint: 6 months (phase 2 pilot UK-HARP-II, ezetimibe 10 mg added to simvastatin 20 mg vs simvastatin 20 mg + placebo)
biomarker_effects.quote: Allocation to simvastatin plus ezetimibe produced an additional 18-mg/dL (0.47-mmol/L) decrease in LDL cholesterol level, representing an incremental 21% reduction over that achieved with simvastatin monotherapy (P < 0.0001).
biomarker_effects.note: n=203 CKD patients. Ezetimibe increment over simvastatin (ezetimibe-placebo controlled). Simvastatin alone: '31-mg/dL (0.8-mmol/L) decrease ... compared with baseline' (not placebo-controlled). No significant effect on TG or HDL-C. Published 2006, before readout.

biomarker_effects.quote: There were no statistically significant effects of the addition of ezetimibe to simvastatin on triglyceride or high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels.
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 3 HDL-C / TG / apoB / non-HDL-C changes: NOT FOUND in SHARP main text (webappendix not accessed).

biomarker_effects.quote: and triglyceride levels by 13% (166 mg/dL [1.87 mmol/L] versus 186 mg/dL [2.10 mmol/L]; P < 0.01)
biomarker_effects.note: Simvastatin alone. Phase 3 TG change NOT FOUND.

hr.unit: rate ratio (key outcome: major atherosclerotic events, log-rank)
hr.quote: 526 (11·3%) first major atherosclerotic events (non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary death, non-haemorrhagic stroke, or arterial revascularisation) among the 4650 participants allocated simvastatin plus ezetimibe compared with 619 (13·4%) among the 4620 allocated placebo, corresponding to a significant 17% proportional reduction (RR 0·83, 95% CI 0·74–0·94; log-rank p=0·0021
hr.note: Registry S3 identical: RR 0.83 (0.74-0.94), log-rank p=0.0021. Original protocol primary (major vascular events, initially randomized only): 639 (15.2%) vs 749 (17.9%), RR 0.84 (0.75-0.93), p=0.001 (S1; S2 '16.1 percent ... (p=0.0010)'). Major vascular events, all randomized: 701 vs 814, RR 0.85 (0.77-0.94), p=0.0012. Components: major coronary events RR 0.92 (0.76-1.11); non-haemorrhagic stroke RR 0.75 (0.60-0.94); arterial revascularisation RR 0.79 (0.68-0.93); all-cause death RR 1.02 (0.94-1.11). S2 reports major atherosclerotic events as '16.5 percent ... (p=0.0022)' (different rounding/model). Per-mmol/L, authors: 'the overall 19% reduction per 1 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction'.

events_treatment.unit: events (patients with first major atherosclerotic event)

safety_signals.value: Myopathy rare: 9 (0.2%) vs 5 (0.1%); rhabdomyolysis 4 vs 1; ~2 excess per 10,000 patient-years
safety_signals.quote: The excess risk of myopathy was only two per 10 000 patients per year of treatment with this combination (9 [0·2%] vs 5 [0·1%]).
safety_signals.note: Study treatment stopped for muscle pain: 49 (1.1%) vs 28 (0.6%), p=0.02 (Table 4).

safety_signals.quote: There was no evidence that simvastatin plus ezetimibe increased the incidence of cancer (438 [9·4%] vs 439 [9·5%], RR 0·99, 95% CI 0·87–1·13, p=0·89; table 3)
safety_signals.note: Addresses the SEAS-derived ezetimibe cancer hypothesis. Cancer deaths 132 (2.8%) vs 114 (2.5%), p=0.26 (Table 3).

safety_signals.value: Non-significant excess of non-vascular deaths: 668 (14.4%) vs 612 (13.2%), RR 1.09 (0.98-1.21); all-cause death RR 1.02 (0.94-1.11)
safety_signals.quote: Simvastatin plus ezetimibe was associated with non-significantly more deaths from any non-vascular cause (668 [14·4%] vs 612 [13·2%]; RR 1·09, 95% CI 0·98–1·21, p=0·13)
safety_signals.note: No significant effect on all-cause mortality: 1142 (24.6%) vs 1115 (24.1%), p=0.63.

safety_signals.value: No excess hepatitis, persistent transaminase rise or gallstones; fewer pancreatitis without gallstones (12 vs 27)
safety_signals.quote: There was no evidence of excess risks of hepatitis (21 [0·5%] vs 18 [0·4%]), gallstones (106 [2·3%] vs 106 [2·3%]), or cancer (438 [9·4%] vs 439 [9·5%], p=0·89)

safety_signals.value: Haemorrhagic stroke non-significantly increased: 45 (1.0%) vs 37 (0.8%), RR 1.21 (0.78-1.86)
safety_signals.quote: There were non-significantly more patients with haemorrhagic stroke (45 [1·0%] vs 37 [0·8%]; RR 1·21, 95% CI 0·78–1·86; p=0·4; webappendix p 2).

safety_signals.value: No effect on kidney disease progression (ESRD) among non-dialysis patients: 1057 (33.9%) vs 1084 (34.6%), RR 0.97 (0.89-1.05)
safety_signals.quote: end-stage renal disease defined as commencement of maintenance dialysis or transplantation (1057 [33·9%] vs 1084 [34·6%]; RR 0·97, 95% CI 0·89–1·05, p=0·41)
safety_signals.note: Efficacy secondary, not a harm; recorded here as a null renal effect.

genetics.finding: 2x2 factorial Mendelian randomization: LDL-C lowering via HMGCR (statin target) and NPC1L1 (ezetimibe target) variants gives the same CHD reduction per unit LDL-C, and the effects are additive
genetics.quote: the NPC1L1 group had 2.4 mg/dl lower LDL-C and 4.8% lower risk of CHD (odds ratio [OR]: 0.952, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.920 to 0.985); whereas the HMGCR group had 2.9 mg/dl lower LDL-C and a similar 5.3% lower risk of CHD (OR: 0.947, 95% CI: 0.909 to 0.986).

genetics.finding: NPC1L1 inactivating mutations (heterozygous) associated with 12 mg/dL lower LDL-C and 53% lower CHD risk
genetics.quote: Heterozygous carriers of NPC1L1 inactivating mutations had a mean LDL cholesterol level that was 12 mg per deciliter (0.31 mmol per liter) lower than that in noncarriers (P=0.04). Carrier status was associated with a relative reduction of 53% in the risk of coronary heart disease (odds ratio for carriers, 0.47; 95% confidence interval, 0.25 to 0.87; P=0.008).

genetics.finding: CTT: major vascular events reduced ~22% per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (calculator benchmark); published 12 days before the SHARP readout
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

genetics.finding: EAS consensus: genetic, epidemiologic and trial evidence establishes that LDL causes ASCVD, with benefit proportional to absolute LDL-C reduction by any mechanism
genetics.quote: Consistent evidence from numerous and multiple different types of clinical and genetic studies unequivocally establishes that LDL causes ASCVD.

consensus_explanation.summary: SHARP met its key outcome: an average LDL-C difference of 0.85 mmol/L (diluted by about two-thirds compliance) over a median 4.9 years gave a 17% reduction in major atherosclerotic events (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.74-0.94), which the investigators judged consistent with the CTT statin relationship per mmol/L, with no excess myopathy, hepatitis, gallstones or cancer. The benefit came from fewer non-haemorrhagic strokes and revascularisations, while major coronary events, vascular and all-cause mortality and CKD progression were not significantly reduced. The main caveat experts drew is the population: in the third of patients on dialysis LDL-C fell less (0.60 vs 0.96 mmol/L) and the effect was smaller and not significant (FDA label: major vascular events RR 0.94, 0.80-1.09 vs 0.78, 0.69-0.89 off dialysis). The CTT 2016 meta-analysis found relative benefit shrinking as eGFR declines with little evidence of benefit on dialysis, so KDIGO 2013 recommends statin or statin/ezetimibe in non-dialysis CKD but not starting statins in most dialysis patients. Lesser caveats: the key outcome was changed before unblinding (the original major-vascular-events endpoint was also significant), and the design could not separate ezetimibe's contribution, so the FDA approved no new indication.

open_questions: Category: success_with_caveats (population caveat: no clear benefit in the dialysis third). robust_success is arguable: upper CI 0.94 (slightly above the ~0.90 guide) and the effect matched the CTT prediction (derived 0.78^0.85 = 0.81 vs observed 0.83); the SHARP investigators themselves argued the dialysis effect was consistent once LDL-C reduction is weighted (per-mmol/L RR 0.84, 0.62-1.13, heterogeneity p=0.25).

Endpoint and population changed before unblinding: from major vascular events in initially randomized patients (sized for 1100 events, 20% RRR, p<0.01) to major atherosclerotic events in all patients ever randomized. Both were significant (RR 0.84, p=0.001 original; RR 0.83, p=0.0021 key). Statistical analysis plan (S4 full text) not read.
Alpha: the power calculation used p<0.01; the final significance threshold and its sidedness for the key outcome were not found (S4 full text not read). Calculator input uses 0.01 two-sided.

LDL-C % change is not given in the Lancet paper; -30% (2.5 years, vs placebo) is from the Merck topline release S2; the 2012 FDA-label release S7 gives 32%. 1-year: 40% (S2) vs 38% (S7). Absolute -0.85 mmol/L (S1) is the ITT average including ~1/3 non-compliance.
apoB, non-HDL-C, HDL-C and triglyceride on-treatment changes in SHARP: NOT FOUND (Lancet webappendix not accessed).

Ezetimibe's own contribution cannot be separated (no simvastatin-alone arm beyond year 1); FDA granted no new indication (S7). target_symbol recorded as HMGCR (simvastatin, the larger LDL-C-lowering component: 26-28% of the 38-40% at 1 year); NPC1L1 (ezetimibe) is the second target.

Lancet editorial (Stevens KK, Jardine AG. 'SHARP: a stab in the right direction in chronic kidney disease', Lancet 2011;377:2153-4, doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(11)60822-2) was found but not read (paywalled, 403); not used as a source.
Topline release S2 was read only through the Wayback Machine capture of 2010-11-24 (no capture on 2010-11-20 itself); the Wayback URL with date 20101120 resolves to it.
